findings.title: Unvalidated ?commit= reaches git argv as an option (diff-tree/show --output writes arbitrary files) via an unguarded GET
findings.rationale: execFileSync with an argv array rules out shell injection, but GET /api/git/file passes req.query.commit straight into fileAt, so commit=--output=/abs/path makes `git diff-tree` open (truncate) that file and `git show` writes to ':'. GET requests skip the write-token guard and project ids are small autoincrement integers, so a cross-site or no-cors fetch at 127.0.0.1 can trigger it without reading the response. The only precondition is that the project path is a git repo.
findings.remediation: Reject any commit that is not a hex object id before calling git, and put --end-of-options before revision arguments in every git call that takes a revision from a request.

findings.title: Per-boot write token served to any Host header (no DNS-rebinding defense)
findings.rationale: The CSRF model is sound for classic cross-origin attacks: the server binds 127.0.0.1 only, sends no CORS headers, and requires a per-boot randomUUID header on every non-GET. It relies on the same-origin policy, though, and neither the standalone Express server nor the API checks Host or Origin, so a DNS-rebinding page that becomes same-origin with 127.0.0.1:41730 can read /api/write-token and then every transcript and mutating route. Vite's allowedHosts likely covers `npm run dev`; the standalone/npx path has no such check.
findings.remediation: Add a Host allowlist middleware (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1] on the bound port) in front of all /api routes, the token route included, and optionally require Origin to match on non-GET requests.

findings.title: GET /api/scan walks any directory named in ?dir= without the write token
findings.rationale: The manual directory scan takes an absolute path from the query string and runs the source parser's filesystem walk over it, with only an existsSync check. Because it is a GET, it is exempt from the write-token guard. Cross-origin pages cannot read the response, so today it is at most a timing/DoS lever, but combined with DNS rebinding (chr-2) it lists log files anywhere the user can read. The POST /import path already requires the token.
findings.remediation: Require the write token (or a same-origin Host/Origin check) for a scan with a caller-supplied dir, and consider resolving it with realpath under the user's home.

findings.title: Explore SQL is built with template literals, but every interpolated fragment comes from an allowlist
findings.snippet: const rr = getDb().prepare(`SELECT ${bm} AS bkt, ${g.col} AS gk, COUNT(*) AS c FROM messages m ${datedBase} ${g.where} GROUP BY bkt, gk`).all(...bind()) as unknown as { bkt: string|null; gk: string|number; c: number }[];
findings.rationale: Queries such as this interpolate ${bm}, ${g.col} and ${g.where} into SQL. Those values come from bucketExpr and groupExpr switch statements with fixed strings, and routes/explore.ts rejects any ?group=/?subgroup= outside GROUPS before this code runs, while user values go through ? binds. There is no injectable path today; this note is only about keeping it that way.
findings.remediation: Keep interpolated SQL limited to switch-derived constants, and add a regression test asserting that unknown group/rollup values throw before any prepare().

findings.title: Ask runner is well confined; the question travels in process argv
findings.rationale: The spawn uses process.execPath with an argv array and no shell. The route requires the write token, enforces a 2000-char limit and a single in-flight run, and kills the whole detached process group on timeout. The residual issue is that the operator's question sits in argv, visible to other local users via ps; the runner already accepts CHRONICLE_ASK_QUESTION from env.
findings.remediation: Pass the question to the runner through the environment (or stdin) rather than argv.

findings.title: Claude OAuth token sent to a hard-coded issuer URL; redirects are followed by default
findings.snippet: const res = await fetch(USAGE_URL, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'anthropic-beta': 'oauth-2025-04-20' }, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS) });
findings.rationale: The OAuth access token is read from the Keychain or ~/.claude/.credentials.json. It is sent only to the constant https://api.anthropic.com URL, is never stored or logged, and the call can be turned off in Settings. fetch follows redirects by default; current undici drops Authorization on cross-origin redirects, so exposure depends on runtime behavior rather than an explicit policy.
findings.remediation: Set redirect: 'error' on the usage fetch so the bearer token can never follow a redirect.
